summary: Creates a registry for smime-type Content-Type parameter values, registers current values, and sets rules for new ones. This makes it easier to find and add values.

eli5.summary: A notebook for the kinds of secure mail labels.

subtitle: A central registry for S/MIME content type labels.

tldr.problem: S/MIME defined a content-type parameter called smime-type with values scattered across multiple RFCs, and more values were being added without a central place to document them.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7114 creates an IANA registry for smime-type parameter values, registers the current values from existing RFCs, and sets a policy for registering new ones.
tldr.outcome: All smime-type values are now documented in one place, and new values can be registered following a clear process.

today: RFC 7114 is a Proposed Standard. The smime-type parameter registry it created is maintained by IANA and remains the central source for S/MIME content type labels.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) defined a Content-Type parameter called smime-type with four original values. Over time, other RFCs like RFC 5273 (Certificate Management over CMS), RFC 2634 (Enhanced Security Services) and RFC 3854 (Securing X.400 Content) added more values. When RFC 7030 (Enrollment over Secure Transport) added another value, it became clear that a registry was needed to keep track of all these values.
sections.eli5: Secure mail kept getting new label types in different documents. This RFC says it's time to write them all in one notebook.

sections.title: The smime-type Registry
sections.content:
IANA created a new registry for smime-type parameter values. The initial registry includes ten values such as certs-only, compressed-data, enveloped-data, signed-data, and others, each with a reference to the RFC that defined it.

New values can be registered using the Specification Required policy, meaning anyone can propose a new value if they have an RFC specifying how it works. The guidelines from RFC 5751 apply to assigning these values.
sections.eli5: The notebook now has ten kinds of secure email labels already in it. If someone invents a new kind, they can add it to the list if they explain how it works.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: RFC 7114 is a Proposed Standard that establishes the permanent registry for smime-type parameter values, which is maintained by IANA.
sections.eli5: This is the official rule book for the secure email label registry.
